chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Samurah ibn Abu Sa'id, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) set out on the she-camel of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and we went out with him walking until he reached the place of the fish sellers. He gathered them and then said, 'Do you know for what reason I have gathered you?' They said, 'No.' He said, 'Do not buy the jirith, nor the marmahi, nor the tafi, nor sell it.'

key_terms.اَلطَّافِيَ: A specific type of fish (likely a bottom-dweller or distinct species)
key_terms.اَلْجِرِيثَ: A specific type of fish (likely a large or distinct species)
key_terms.اَلْمَارْمَاهِيَ: A specific type of fish (likely mackerel or similar)
key_terms.بَغْلَةِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ: The she-camel of the Messenger of God

ai.seo_question: What specific types of fish did Imam Ali prohibit buying and selling?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records Imam Ali (peace be upon him) issuing a specific commercial prohibition on the trade of *jirith*, *marmahi*, and *tafi* fish, likely due to their distinct physical characteristics or suitability for consumption. The ruling highlights the early Shia jurisprudential approach to defining permissible (*halal*) and impermissible (*haram*) marine life, emphasizing that commercial validity depends on the specific attributes of the species rather than a general category.
